members.title: Fire at NCP MP Nusrat’s family home in Kushtia; petrol bomb attack alleged
members.lead: A fire broke out at the family home of Nusrat Tabassum, an MP elected to a reserved seat for women and a leader of the National Citizen Party (NCP), in Kushtia. NCP leaders have alleged that petrol bombs were hurled at the house. The fire broke out shortly after midnight on Wednesday at Nusrat’s ancestral home in Bagoyan village in Daulatpur upazila of Kushtia. Delwar Hossain, additional superintendent of police (Bheramara Circle), told Prothom Alo that firefighters rushed to the scene after receiving the report and brought the blaze under control at around 1.50 am. By then, however, considerable damage had been caused. Five of the eight rooms in the single-storey tin-roofed house were gutted. Two goats were also burnt to death. . Police officer Delwar Hossain added that Nusrat Tabassum’s parents live on the second floor of a separate three-storey building, 10 to 15 yards away from the house. That building was unaffected by the fire. No member of the MP’s family sustained burn injuries. Nusrat Tabassum is an NCP joint convener and a member of the party’s Political Council, its highest policy-making body. She is also a member of the 13th parliament representing a reserved seat for women. In a Facebook post, the NCP’s media cell alleged that Awami League goons had hurled petrol bombs at her house. Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, the party’s spokesperson, also alleged in a Facebook post that a petrol bomb attack had been carried out on Nusrat Tabassum’s home. When Prothom Alo called Nusrat Tabassum’s personal mobile number for comment, the call was answered by Wahiduzzaman, the NCP’s deputy secretary for youth and employment affairs. At around 2:00 am, he said that he was travelling from Dhaka to Kushtia in the same vehicle as MP Nusrat Tabassum after they received news of the incident. . Describing the attack, Wahiduzzaman told Prothom Alo, “Shortly after midnight, the ancestral and permanent residence of the MP in Bagoyan village of Daulatpur upazila, Kushtia, was target…

members.title: ‘Today me, tomorrow you, day after everyone else will be attacked’: Nahid Islam
members.lead: The “fallen criminal fascist forces” are targeting the leaders and stakeholders of the July Revolution, said Nahid Islam, convener of National Citizen Party (NCP). “When one falls, all are at risk. Today it is me, tomorrow it could be you and the day after, everyone else will be attacked one by one,” he said. The opposition chief whip made the remarks in a post on his verified Facebook page at around 3:00 am on Thursday. .Fire at NCP MP Nusrat’s family home in Kushtia; petrol bomb attack alleged. In the post, the NCP convener said he no longer expected the government and administration to be able to provide security to the people. “We have to choose our own way,” he wrote. Nahid Islam said, fascist Awami League is not a domestic force. Backed, sheltered and instigated by Delhi, the anti-July forces are tearing Bangladesh apart. They carry out sabotage inside the country and cross the border to take shelter on the other side, he wrote. . Saying they would confront anti-Bangladesh forces, Nahid wrote, “We will do so unitedly and democratically.” NCP leaders have alleged that a petrol bomb was thrown at the village home of party leader and reserved-seat member of parliament (MP) Nusrat Tabassum in Kushtia. A fire broke out at her family home in Bagowan village under Daulatpur upazila of Kushtia shortly after midnight on Thursday. .NCP wants to keep Jamaat ‘in line’ while remaining in alliance. Nusrat is a joint convener of the NCP and a member of its highest policymaking forum, the Political Council. She is also a member of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad from a reserved women's seat. In a Facebook post, the NCP Media Cell alleged that Awami League activists had hurled a petrol bomb at her home. NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain also said in a Facebook post that a petrol bomb attack had been carried out on Nusrat Tabassum's house.
